newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST- Yield set to rise on Portugal 3-yr bonds.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Yield set to rise on Portugal 3-yr bonds.

text.p: The average yield in the Institute for Public Credit Management's (IGCP) auction of 25 billion escudos ($147.7 million) of three-year bonds was seen between 5.45 and 5.50 percent, in line with the secondary market but up from 5.386 percent at the last such sale.
On January 27, the Institute placed 28.5 billion escudos of the March 2000 paper.
Results of Wednesday's sale were expected shortly after 1100 GMT.
Analysts said they did not expect aggressive bidding because of some nervousness before January inflation data are released and the Institute's next auction on Friday.
The National Statistics Institute has not yet given a date for the release of the January inflation numbers, but they are expected within the next few days.

"The auction is going to be in line with the secondary market -- 5.45 to 5.50 percent," said one analyst. "Below 5.45 percent is difficult and above 5.50 percent would not, I think, be accepted by the IGCP," he added.
There was no trade in the March 2000 on Monday, but the April 2000 closed at 5.47 percent, two basis points above the Spanish April 2000 equivalent.
